content.identity:
Zoltan Sternovsky is a full Professor jointly appointed to the Ann and H.J. Smead Aerospace Engineering Sciences department and the Laboratory for Atmospheric and Space Physics (LASP) at the University of Colorado Boulder. The official faculty page lists him as "Professor" - "LABORATORY FOR ATMOSPHERICS AND SPACE PHYSICS (LASP)", contact `Zoltan.Sternovsky@colorado.edu`, phone 303-735-6272, and a research agenda spanning "cosmic dust, lunar plasma and dust environment, physics of dusty plasmas, plasma diagnostics, dust charging, laboratory plasma physics, plasma simulations; mesospheric aerosol particles; instrument development for sounding rockets and satellites" ([identity[0]] [2]). His CV trajectory - MS in Physics (1998) and PhD in Physics of Ionized Media (2001) from Charles University, Prague; Research Scientist at LASP from 2005; tenure-track progression Assistant Professor (2009-2015) to Associate Professor (2015-2024) to Professor (since 2024) - is consistent with the topic scope given in the lead ([identity[0]] [2]).

LASP's own People page independently corroborates the role and adds a specific mission-instrument history: "Tenure Track Faculty... instrument scientist on two sounding rocket campaigns, and several space missions, including the Lunar Dust EXperiment (LDEX) instrument launched onboard Lunar Atmosphere and Dust Environment Explorer (LADEE) spacecraft, the Surface Dust Analyzer (SUDA) onboard the Europa Clipper flagship mission, and the Interstellar Dust Experiment (IDEX) instrument onboard the Interstellar Mapping and Acceleration Probe (IMAP) mission" ([identity[1]] [75]). The independent CU Experts directory lists positions verbatim as "Professor, Laboratory for Atmospheric and Space Physics (LASP)" and "Professor, Aerospace Engineering Sciences" ([identity[2]] [93]). ORCID 0000-0002-9658-1350 is his registered identifier ([identity[3]] [48]). No namesake collision: the only same-name noise surfaced was a "Zoltan Homes" custom builder in Florida ([identity[4]] [57]) and a LinkedIn profile for a different person - the LinkedIn slug `zoltan-sternovsky-67301643` resolves to the same individual and is internally consistent with the email, institutional address, and bio.

**Insight -> mechanism -> implication**: All three first-party profiles agree he is a full Professor (since 2024) within LASP/Aerospace, not a Research Scientist or Assistant Professor as the stale LinkedIn label implies. The institutional record is the authoritative source; LinkedIn is the lagging indicator.
